description:
src/lib.rs:140 — `pub const AIA_MAX_DEPTH: usize = 5;` is exposed in
the public surface, but `Verifier` provides no way to override it.
A caller wanting one of:

- a *lower* cap (defense-in-depth: \"I trust at most 1 hop of AIA
  fetching against my well-known PKI\")
- a *higher* cap for an unusual deep-cross-sign environment
- runtime-configurable cap based on caller policy

cannot configure it through any pkix-chain API. The only escape hatch
is to skip `verify_one` entirely and call
`pkix_path_builder::build_first_valid_path` directly with their own
AIA loop — which loses all the wrapper logic.

This is the worst of both worlds: the constant is `pub` (so it's a
forever-stable item in the API surface and changing its value is a
soft breaking change for callers comparing depths) AND immutable for
callers wanting to deviate.

Three reasonable fixes:

a) Add an override on `Verifier`:

       impl Verifier { pub fn with_aia_max_depth(mut self, depth: usize) -> Self }

   `AIA_MAX_DEPTH` stays as the documented default. Callers opt into
   a different value if they want.

b) Promote it to a configurable field on `ValidationPolicy` (since
   that's already where time / max_path_len / etc. live). Keeps the
   pkix-chain API stable; callers tune via the existing policy
   surface.

c) De-pub the constant (drop the `pub`) and keep it as an internal
   implementation detail. Callers who care about the value learn it
   from the `Error::AiaDepthExceeded` Display string. Simplest;
   removes the contract entirely.

(b) is most consistent with the rest of the workspace. (a) is the
smallest change to the current shape. (c) is the punt.

PKIX-q9hv.1 separately notes the off-by-one bug in how the cap is
applied; fixing that bug first is sensible — but the override question
stands either way.

Caller impact: anyone with non-default trust-domain depth requirements.
title: AIA_MAX_DEPTH is pub const with no Verifier-level override
